predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: the Brittonic coast between the Forth and the Tees before Ida

successors.name: Kingdom of Northumbria
successors.text: Bernicia united with Deira under Oswald

ledger.x: 547: Ida takes the throne of Bernicia, probably at Bamburgh.

c. 604: Æthelfrith takes Deira under his crown. 'Æthelfrith united Deira with his own kingdom by force around 604' and the infobox has 'Shared crown with Deira: 604'; the page adds 'It is unknown when the Angles finally conquered the whole region, but around 604 is likely.' Typed…
612: Deira's separate status under the Bernician crown ends on the map as Cliopatria's Northumbria row begins.
612: Bernicia's land passes into Cliopatria's Northumbria shape, which runs 612-632; the bridge that hands the land over before the 633 gain.
633: Bernicia stands alone again under Eanfrith.
634: Oswald reunites Bernicia and Deira as Northumbria.

wars.name: Urien of Rheged's siege of Lindisfarne
wars.outcome: Urien 'penned the Anglo-Saxons in at Lindisfarne' and Theodric was 'besieged ... on Lindisfarne'; Urien was then killed at the instigation of Morgan (Morcant).

wars.name: Battle of Catraeth
wars.outcome: 'In around 600 the Gododdin raised a force of about 300 men to assault the Angle stronghold of Catraeth, perhaps Catterick, North Yorkshire.

wars.name: Battle of Degsastan
wars.outcome: Bede reports Æthelfrith won 'a crushing victory at a place called Degsastan' over Áedán mac Gabráin of Dál Riata, who led 'an immense and mighty army'.

wars.name: Battle of Chester
wars.outcome: Æthelfrith 'defeated its army in a battle at Chester', probably between 613 and 616; no land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Battle of the River Idle
wars.outcome: 'around 616 Æthelfrith was defeated and killed at the Battle of the River Idle'; Edwin 'became king not just of Deira but of Bernicia as well'.

wars.name: Battle of Heavenfield
wars.outcome: Oswald 'finally defeated Cadwallon at the Battle of Heavenfield in 634' and united Bernicia with Deira.

certainty.note: The Forth, Tees and Pennine frontiers are approximate; no source fixes a line.
